claim: TFIID is a complex of TATA-binding protein (TBP) and TBP-associated factors (TAFs).
source: TFIID—a complex of TATA-binding protein (TBP) and TBP-associated factors (TAFs)—is a central component of the Pol II promoter recognition apparatus.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as established background knowledge about TFIID composition.

claim: TFIID is a central component of the Pol II promoter recognition apparatus.
source: TFIID—a complex of TATA-binding protein (TBP) and TBP-associated factors (TAFs)—is a central component of the Pol II promoter recognition apparatus.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TFIID's role in transcription.

claim: TFIID subunits are significantly downregulated in terminally differentiated myocytes, hepatocytes and adipocytes.
source: Recent studies have revealed significant downregulation of TFIID subunits in terminally differentiated myocytes, hepatocytes and adipocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies in the field.

claim: TBP protein levels are tightly regulated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: Here, we report that TBP protein levels are tightly regulated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Huwe1 is an E3 ligase targeting TBP for K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: Using an in vitro ubiquitination assay coupled with biochemical fractionation, we identified Huwe1 as an E3 ligase targeting TBP for K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasome-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by biochemical fractionation data (Figure 2) and in vitro ubiquitination assays (Figure 3).

claim: Upregulation of Huwe1 expression during myogenesis induces TBP degradation and myotube differentiation.
source: Upregulation of Huwe1 expression during myogenesis induces TBP degradation and myotube differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing Huwe1 upregulation during differentiation (Figure 5B) and effects of Huwe1 knockdown on differentiation (Figure 6).

claim: Huwe1 activity on TBP is antagonized by the deubiquitinase USP10.
source: We found that Huwe1 activity on TBP is antagonized by the deubiquitinase USP10, which protects TBP from degradation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing USP10 reduces TBP ubiquitination (Figure 7A) and increases TBP protein levels (Figure 7C).

claim: USP10 protects TBP from degradation.
source: We found that Huwe1 activity on TBP is antagonized by the deubiquitinase USP10, which protects TBP from degradation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing USP10 overexpression increases TBP protein levels and half-life.

claim: Modulating the levels of both Huwe1 and USP10 fine-tunes the requisite degradation of TBP during myogenesis.
source: Thus, modulating the levels of both Huwe1 and USP10 appears to fine-tune the requisite degradation of TBP during myogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing Huwe1 upregulation and USP10 downregulation during differentiation.

claim: TBP serves as a key subunit to facilitate transcription initiation by all three RNA polymerases in eukaryotic cells.
source: TBP serves as a key subunit to facilitate transcription initiation by all three RNA polymerases in eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TBP's role in transcription.

claim: TBP and its associated factors (TAFs) that make up the TFIID complex are specific for Pol II-mediated mRNA transcription.
source: Similarly, TBP and its associated factors (TAFs) that make up the TFIID complex are specific for Pol II-mediated mRNA transcription (Dynlacht et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: TBP plays a role in recognizing Pol I-transcribed promoters as part of the SL1 complex.
source: As a part of the SL1 complex, TBP plays a role in recognizing Pol I-transcribed promoters (Comai et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The TBP/B/BRF complex TFIIIB drives the transcription of small nuclear RNAs by Pol III.
source: Likewise, the TBP/B/BRF complex TFIIIB drives the transcription of small nuclear RNAs by Pol III (Taggart et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Reductions in TBP protein levels are much more pronounced than decreases in its mRNA levels during terminal differentiation.
source: Interestingly, it was found that reductions in TBP protein levels are much more pronounced than decreases in its mRNA levels, suggesting that an important level of TBP regulation occurs post-transcriptionally (Deato and Tjian, 2007; D'Alessio et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013; Herrera et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: An important level of TBP regulation occurs post-transcriptionally.
source: Interestingly, it was found that reductions in TBP protein levels are much more pronounced than decreases in its mRNA levels, suggesting that an important level of TBP regulation occurs post-transcriptionally (Deato and Tjian, 2007; D'Alessio et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013; Herrera et al., 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that protein levels decrease more than mRNA levels.

claim: Upon myogenic differentiation of C2C12 cells, TBP protein levels become significantly downregulated while its mRNA levels remained largely unchanged.
source: Consistent with several earlier observations from our lab and other studies (Perletti et al., 1999; Deato and Tjian, 2007), we found that upon myogenic differentiation of C2C12 cells TBP protein levels become significantly downregulated, while its mRNA levels remained largely unchanged (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that TBP downregulation mainly occurs via modulation of its protein levels.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citations to previous studies.

claim: TBP downregulation during myogenic differentiation mainly occurs via modulation of its protein levels.
source: Consistent with several earlier observations from our lab and other studies (Perletti et al., 1999; Deato and Tjian, 2007), we found that upon myogenic differentiation of C2C12 cells TBP protein levels become significantly downregulated, while its mRNA levels remained largely unchanged (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that TBP downregulation mainly occurs via modulation of its protein levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that protein levels decrease more than mRNA levels.

claim: Treatment of differentiated C2C12 myotubes with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 partially restores TBP protein levels within 4 hr.
source: Strikingly, TBP protein levels were partially restored within 4 hr after MG132 treatment (Figure 1A), suggesting that the UPS likely plays a dominant role in regulating TBP levels during terminal differentiation.
evidence: This is directly shown in the western blot data in Figure 1A.

claim: The ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) plays a dominant role in regulating TBP levels during terminal differentiation.
source: Strikingly, TBP protein levels were partially restored within 4 hr after MG132 treatment (Figure 1A), suggesting that the UPS likely plays a dominant role in regulating TBP levels during terminal differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that proteasome inhibition restores TBP levels.

claim: TBP is ubiquitinated in vivo.
source: Western blot analysis confirmed the presence of slower-migrating poly-ubiquitinated species of the TBP protein in the pull-downs, suggesting TBP is indeed ubiquitinated in cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly shown by the in vivo ubiquitination assay data in Figure 1B.

claim: TBP can be ubiquitinated by both C2C12 myoblast and myotube whole cell extracts in vitro.
source: Higher molecular weight ubiquitinated TBP species were detected in reactions with both myoblast and myotube lysates, suggesting TBP ubiquitination activities are present in both proliferating muscle progenitors and terminally differentiated muscle cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly shown by the in vitro ubiquitination assay data in Figure 1C.

claim: TBP ubiquitination activities are present in both proliferating muscle progenitors and terminally differentiated muscle cells.
source: Higher molecular weight ubiquitinated TBP species were detected in reactions with both myoblast and myotube lysates, suggesting TBP ubiquitination activities are present in both proliferating muscle progenitors and terminally differentiated muscle cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the detection of ubiquitinated TBP in both cell types.

claim: TBP can be ubiquitinated by lysates of Hela cells.
source: We detected significant TBP ubiquitination activities in Hela whole cell extracts (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly shown by the in vitro ubiquitination assay data in Figure 2A.

claim: Most of the TBP ubiquitination activities in HeLa cells are present in the cytoplasmic fraction (S100).
source: We then separated the whole cell extract into cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions, and found that most of the TBP ubiquitination activities were present in the cytoplasmic fraction (S100) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly shown by comparing activities in different fractions in Figure 2A.

claim: GST-TBP but not GST is ubiquitinated in the in vitro ubiquitination reaction.
source: It is worth noting that while GST-TBP can be efficiently ubiquitinated in the reaction, we did not detect any ubiquitination of the GST protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that these ubiquitination activities are specific to TBP.
evidence: This is directly shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The ubiquitination activities detected in the assay are specific to TBP.
source: It is worth noting that while GST-TBP can be efficiently ubiquitinated in the reaction, we did not detect any ubiquitination of the GST protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that these ubiquitination activities are specific to TBP.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GST alone is not ubiquitinated.

claim: The TBP E3 ligase has an approximate molecular mass of 440–660 kDa.
source: Ubiquitination assays on the activities eluted from the Superose 6 sizing column suggest the molecular weight of the E3 ligase(s) to be about 440–660 kDa (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is determined by gel filtration chromatography data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Huwe1 protein consists of 4374 amino acids with a molecular mass of around 480 kDa.
source: Moreover, Huwe1 protein consists of 4374 amino acids with a molecular mass of around 480 kDa (Chen et al., 2005; Zhong et al., 2005), consistent with the molecular weight predicted for the TBP E3 ligase activity after Superose 6 gel filtration (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies characterizing Huwe1.

claim: The molecular mass of Huwe1 is consistent with the molecular weight predicted for the TBP E3 ligase activity after Superose 6 gel filtration.
source: Moreover, Huwe1 protein consists of 4374 amino acids with a molecular mass of around 480 kDa (Chen et al., 2005; Zhong et al., 2005), consistent with the molecular weight predicted for the TBP E3 ligase activity after Superose 6 gel filtration (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is inferred by comparing the known size of Huwe1 with the gel filtration results.

claim: The abundance of Huwe1 protein positively correlates with levels of TBP E3 ligase activity within selected MonoQ fractions.
source: Specifically, a total of 81 Huwe1 peptides (18.4% coverage) were detected in fractions with the highest E3 activities, and this number fell to 30 and 14 peptides in the fractions with intermediate and low E3 activities, respectively.
evidence: This is shown by the Mudpit mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 2F.

claim: Purified recombinant Huwe1 mediates dose-dependent poly-ubiquitination of TBP in vitro.
source: To test whether Huwe1 indeed mediates TBP ubiquitination, we performed in vitro ubiquitination assays with purified recombinant Huwe1 proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), which resulted in a dose-dependent poly-ubiquitination of TBP detected as high molecular weight species using anti-TBP antibody (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly shown by the in vitro ubiquitination assay data in Figure 3A.

claim: TBP has more than 10 distinct ubiquitination sites.
source: Since these shifted bands likely correspond to different ubiquitination sites, the use of methyl ubiquitin also allowed us to estimate the number of distinct ubiquitination sites on TBP to be more than 10 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from the ladder pattern observed with methyl ubiquitin in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The HECT domain of Huwe1 is required for its TBP ubiquitination activity.
source: To confirm that the HECT domain of Huwe1 is required for its TBP ubiquitination activity, we generated two mutants of Huwe1: one with the HECT domain truncated (Δ4341–4374), the other with the active site cysteine residue mutated to serine. Both mutant proteins were purified through the same procedures as the wild type protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A). Neither of the mutants was able to mediate TBP ubiquitination in vitro (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is directly shown by comparing wild-type and mutant Huwe1 activities in Figure 3B.

claim: The N-terminal region of Huwe1 outside the catalytic domain is required for efficient TBP ubiquitination.
source: Apparently, the N-terminal region of Huwe1 outside the catalytic domain is also required for efficient TBP ubiquitination, as the homologous HECT domain from E3 ligase E6AP was unable to carry out TBP ubiquitination (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that E6AP HECT domain cannot ubiquitinate TBP, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Both the UbcH5 family E2s and UbcH7 are active in the in vitro ubiquitination assay with recombinant purified Huwe1.
source: We therefore tested the ability of a panel of E2s to collaborate with Huwe1 in mediating TBP ubiquitination, and found that both the UbcH5 family E2s and UbcH7 are active in the in vitro ubiquitination assay with recombinant purified Huwe1 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), consistent with the E2 enzymes that worked with the crude 0.3 M KCl fraction from the D52 column.
evidence: This is directly shown by testing different E2s in Figure 3D.

claim: Huwe1 mediates K48-linked ubiquitin chain formation on TBP.
source: Strikingly, when K48R ubiquitin was used, poly-ubiquitinated TBP species were significantly diminished (Figure 3E, lane 4), suggesting that Huwe1 likely mediates K48-linked ubiquitin chain formation on TBP.
evidence: This is shown by testing ubiquitin mutants in Figure 3E.

claim: K48-linked ubiquitin chains usually lead to proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: Ubiquitin chains of this topology usually lead to proteasome-mediated degradation (Komander and Rape, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Knocking-down Huwe1 in 293T cells with two different shRNAs results in increased levels of endogenous TBP protein.
source: Knocking-down Huwe1 in 293T cells with two different shRNAs resulted in increased levels of endogenous TBP protein (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: Knockdown of Huwe1 by 2 independent shRNAs leads to significant increases in mCherry/GFP intensity ratios of the TBP-fluorescent timer fusion protein.
source: Knockdown of Huwe1 by 2 independent shRNAs led to significant increases in mCherry/GFP intensity ratios, evident in both imaging and flow cytometry analysis (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is directly shown by fluorescence imaging and flow cytometry data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Lentivirus-mediated Huwe1 shRNA knockdown in C2C12 myoblasts leads to elevated endogenous TBP protein levels.
source: Similarly, lentivirus-mediated Huwe1 shRNA knockdown in C2C12 myoblasts leads to elevated endogenous TBP protein levels (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 5A.

claim: Huwe1 knockdown by two independent shRNAs increases TBP protein half-life in myoblasts.
source: Consistent with results from fluorescent timer experiments, Huwe1 knockdown by two independent shRNAs both increased TBP protein half-life in myoblasts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by cycloheximide chase experiments in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Huwe1 modulates TBP protein levels in living cells.
source: Taken together, our results strongly suggest that Huwe1 modulates TBP protein levels in living cells.
evidence: This is inferred from multiple experiments showing effects of Huwe1 knockdown on TBP levels and half-life.

claim: Huwe1 protein levels are significantly upregulated in myotubes compared to myoblasts.
source: Strikingly, in contrast to dramatic decreases in TBP protein levels, Huwe1 protein levels are significantly upregulated in myotubes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 5B.

claim: Huwe1 transcripts are enriched in muscle tissues.
source: This observation is consistent with previously published results showing that Huwe1 transcripts are enriched in muscle tissues (Schwarz et al., 1998; Chen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Treatment of myotubes with high titer viruses expressing shRNAs against Huwe1 on differentiation Day 4 results in abnormal morphologies of the polynucleated myotubes.
source: To confirm that Huwe1 is indeed responsible for active TBP degradation in myotubes, we treated myotubes with high titer viruses expressing shRNAs against Huwe1 on differentiation Day 4. This treatment resulted in abnormal morphologies of the polynucleated myotubes (Figure 6D), accompanied by increased TBP protein levels (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is directly shown by phase contrast images in Figure 6D.

claim: Huwe1 knockdown in differentiated myotubes increases TBP protein levels.
source: To confirm that Huwe1 is indeed responsible for active TBP degradation in myotubes, we treated myotubes with high titer viruses expressing shRNAs against Huwe1 on differentiation Day 4. This treatment resulted in abnormal morphologies of the polynucleated myotubes (Figure 6D), accompanied by increased TBP protein levels (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 5C.

claim: Upregulation of Huwe1 protein levels during myogenesis leads to enhanced TBP ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of TBP protein.
source: These results support a model wherein the upregulation of Huwe1 protein levels during myogenesis likely leads to enhanced TBP ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of TBP protein.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between Huwe1 upregulation and TBP downregulation during differentiation.

claim: Huwe1 knockdown cells fail to differentiate into polynucleated myotubes efficiently even after 6 days of differentiation.
source: Interestingly, Huwe1 knockdown cells failed to differentiate into polynucleated myotubes efficiently even after 6 days of differentiation (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is directly shown by phase contrast images in Figure 6A.

claim: The induction of several master myogenic regulators (Myod1, Myog and Mef2c) is inhibited in Huwe1 knockdown cells during differentiation.
source: Consistent with this phenotypic observation, the induction of several master myogenic regulators (Myod1, Myog and Mef2c) was inhibited in the Huwe1 knockdown cells during differentiation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Many genes critical for muscle development have lower expression levels in Huwe1 knockdown cells on differentiation Day 6.
source: Differential gene expression followed by gene ontology analysis revealed that many genes critical for muscle development have lower expression levels in Huwe1 knockdown cells (e.g., Myod1, Myog, Mef2a, Mef2c, Ckm and Myh3) on differentiation Day 6 (Figure 6B,C; Figure 6—source data 1), suggesting the functional importance of Huwe1 during in vitro muscle differentiation.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq differential expression analysis in Figure 6B,C.

claim: Huwe1 is functionally important during in vitro muscle differentiation.
source: Differential gene expression followed by gene ontology analysis revealed that many genes critical for muscle development have lower expression levels in Huwe1 knockdown cells (e.g., Myod1, Myog, Mef2a, Mef2c, Ckm and Myh3) on differentiation Day 6 (Figure 6B,C; Figure 6—source data 1), suggesting the functional importance of Huwe1 during in vitro muscle differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the effects of Huwe1 knockdown on muscle gene expression and differentiation.

claim: Loss of Huwe1 in differentiated myotubes induces abnormal morphological changes.
source: We further tested this notion by directly knocking down Huwe1 in differentiated myotubes. Loss of Huwe1 induced abnormal morphological changes of myotubes (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is directly shown by phase contrast images in Figure 6D.

claim: Many genes important for muscle development are downregulated in Huwe1 depleted myotubes.
source: Consistent with these morphological changes, differential gene expression followed by gene ontology analysis revealed that many genes (e.g., Myog, Mef2a, Mef2c, Ckm and Myh3) important for muscle development are downregulated in Huwe1 depleted myotubes (Figure 6E,F; Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq differential expression analysis in Figure 6E,F.

claim: Ubp3 deubiquitinates Tbp1 both in vivo and in vitro in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and prevents Tbp1 from proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: Interestingly, a previous study reported that in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Ubp3 deubiquitinates Tbp1 both in vivo and in vitro and prevents Tbp1 from proteasome-mediated degradation (Chew et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: USP10 is the likely mammalian homolog of yeast Ubp3.
source: A protein sequence homology comparison suggests that ubiquitin-specific protease 10 (USP10) is the likely mammalian homolog of Ubp3 (Cohen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study on protein homology.

claim: Overexpression of USP10 significantly inhibits TBP ubiquitination in 293T cells.
source: To test whether USP10 deubiquitinates and stabilizes TBP in mammalian cells, we overexpressed USP10 in 293T cells and monitored TBP ubiquitination levels in these cells. Strikingly, overexpression of USP10 significantly inhibited TBP ubiquitination (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is directly shown by in vivo ubiquitination assay data in Figure 7A.

claim: TBP can co-immunoprecipitate with USP10.
source: To test whether USP10 deubiquitinates TBP through direct protein–protein interactions, we used HA-TBP to co-IP with Flag-USP10 co-expressed in 293T cells. Our experiment revealed that TBP can co-immunoprecipitate with USP10 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is directly shown by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 7B.

claim: USP10 overexpression modestly increases TBP protein levels in C2C12 myoblasts.
source: Importantly, both western blot and flow cytometry analysis confirmed modestly increased TBP protein levels in a C2C12 stable cell line overexpressing USP10 (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown by western blot and flow cytometry data in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: USP10-mediated TBP deubiquitination contributes to regulating TBP levels during myogenesis.
source: These results suggest that USP10-mediated TBP deubiquitination might also contribute to regulating TBP levels during myogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the effects of USP10 on TBP ubiquitination and protein levels.

claim: The protein levels of USP10 decrease during in vitro muscle differentiation.
source: To further test this possibility, we compared the protein levels of USP10 before and after myotube differentiation. Interestingly, similar to TBP, the protein levels of USP10 decrease during in vitro muscle differentiation (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 7D.

claim: USP10 overexpression in myotubes results in higher levels of TBP protein.
source: Upon addition of the inducer (cumate), USP10 can be induced to higher levels in both myoblasts and myotubes (Figure 7E). USP10 overexpression in myotubes resulted in higher levels of TBP protein (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 7E.

claim: C2C12 cells overexpressing USP10 fail to differentiate into polynucleated myotubes in differentiation medium.
source: To probe whether UPS10 downregulation during myogenesis is of functional significance, we evaluated the differentiation potential of the C2C12 cell line overexpressing USP10. These cells failed to differentiate into polynucleated myotubes in differentiation medium (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is directly shown by phase contrast images in Figure 7F.

claim: Several important myogenic markers fail to be induced in cells overexpressing USP10 even on differentiation Day 6.
source: Consistent with this observation, transcriptome analysis revealed that several important myogenic markers (e.g., Myod1, Myog, Myh3 and Ckm) failed to be induced in cells overexpressing USP10 even on differentiation Day 6 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq differential expression analysis in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A combination of Huwe1 upregulation and USP10 downregulation is important for modulating TBP degradation during myogenesis.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that a combination of Huwe1 upregulation and USP10 downregulation may be important for modulating TBP degradation during myogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the coordinated changes in Huwe1 and USP10 levels during differentiation and their effects on TBP.

claim: The ubiquitin-proteasome system plays a dominant role in mediating TBP protein levels in terminally differentiated myotubes.
source: Here, we show that the ubiquitin-proteasome system plays a dominant role in mediating TBP protein levels in terminally differentiated myotubes.
evidence: This is supported by the MG132 rescue experiment shown in Figure 1A.

claim: An E3 ligase activity responsible for ubiquitinating TBP is present in proliferating cell types such as myoblasts and Hela cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that an E3 ligase activity responsible for ubiquitinating TBP is also present in proliferating cell types such as myoblasts and Hela cells, where TBP is highly expressed.
evidence: This is shown by in vitro ubiquitination assays with myoblast and HeLa lysates in Figures 1C and 2A.

claim: Cellular TBP protein levels are under active surveillance by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: These results suggest that cellular TBP protein levels are under active surveillance by the ubiquitin-proteasome system and that TBP protein levels may be tightly regulated in a cell-type specific manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the presence of ubiquitination activities in both proliferating and differentiated cells.

claim: TBP protein levels may be tightly regulated in a cell-type specific manner.
source: These results suggest that cellular TBP protein levels are under active surveillance by the ubiquitin-proteasome system and that TBP protein levels may be tightly regulated in a cell-type specific manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential regulation of TBP in different cell types.

claim: Deletion of Huwe1 results in embryonic lethality in mice.
source: Huwe1 is essential for animal development. Specifically, deletion of Huwe1 results in embryonic lethality, with knock-out embryos displaying hemorrhage in the abdominal region by embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5), followed by growth impairment, necrosis, and eventual death (Kon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Huwe1 is essential for animal development.
source: Huwe1 is essential for animal development. Specifically, deletion of Huwe1 results in embryonic lethality, with knock-out embryos displaying hemorrhage in the abdominal region by embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5), followed by growth impairment, necrosis, and eventual death (Kon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study showing embryonic lethality.

claim: Huwe1 has been suggested to target several proteins involved in cell-cycle check point and apoptosis, including p53, MCL-1, N-MYC, C-MYC and CDC6.
source: In addition to TBP, Huwe1 has also been suggested to target several other proteins involved in cell-cycle check point and apoptosis, including p53, MCL-1, N-MYC, C-MYC and CDC6.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Huwe1 substrates from previous studies.

claim: USP10 is a ubiquitously expressed deubiquitinase.
source: USP10 is a ubiquitously expressed deubiquitinase, whose substrates include tumor suppressor p53 (Yuan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Substrates of USP10 include tumor suppressor p53.
source: USP10 is a ubiquitously expressed deubiquitinase, whose substrates include tumor suppressor p53 (Yuan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A stable cell line (C2C12) overexpressing USP10 is impaired in myotube formation.
source: However, we found that a stable cell line (C2C12) overexpressing USP10 is impaired in myotube formation, suggesting that down-regulation of USP10 may also be a prerequisite for efficient differentiation of myoblasts into myotubes in culture.
evidence: This is shown by the differentiation experiments in Figure 7F.

claim: Down-regulation of USP10 may be a prerequisite for efficient differentiation of myoblasts into myotubes in culture.
source: However, we found that a stable cell line (C2C12) overexpressing USP10 is impaired in myotube formation, suggesting that down-regulation of USP10 may also be a prerequisite for efficient differentiation of myoblasts into myotubes in culture.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that USP10 overexpression impairs differentiation.

claim: USP10 can recognize ubiquitinated TBP through direct protein–protein interactions.
source: Our immune-precipitation experiments suggest that USP10 can recognize ubiquitinated TBP through direct protein–protein interactions (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 7B.

claim: Down-regulation of TBP should influence cell cycle exit of myoblasts, a key step during myotube differentiation.
source: However, given the seminal role of TFIID/TBP in promoting the transcription of cell cycle and DNA replication genes (Um et al., 2001), it is reasonable to speculate that down-regulation of TBP should at least influence cell cycle exit of myoblasts, a key step during myotube differentiation.
evidence: This is speculated based on known roles of TBP in cell cycle gene transcription.

claim: TFIID/TBP plays a seminal role in promoting the transcription of cell cycle and DNA replication genes.
source: However, given the seminal role of TFIID/TBP in promoting the transcription of cell cycle and DNA replication genes (Um et al., 2001), it is reasonable to speculate that down-regulation of TBP should at least influence cell cycle exit of myoblasts, a key step during myotube differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: TBP protein levels become dramatically reduced in terminally differentiated hepatocytes and adipocytes.
source: Since TBP protein levels also become dramatically reduced in terminally differentiated hepatocytes and adipocytes (D'Alessio et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013), it will also be interesting to test whether Huwe1 and UPS10 contribute to TBP downregulation in these other cell types.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Other components of the TFIID complex become down-regulated during terminal differentiation.
source: In addition to TBP, other components of the TFIID complex also become down-regulated during terminal differentiation, and in the future it will be worth investigating whether they are targeted by the same or different E3/deubiquitinase pairs.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Significant up-regulation of Huwe1 and simultaneous down-regulation of UPS10 during myotube differentiation play an important role in regulating proper TBP protein levels during muscle differentiation.
source: Our results suggest that significant up-regulation of Huwe1 and simultaneous down-regulation of UPS10 during myotube differentiation (Figure 5B, Figure 7D) may play an important role in regulating proper TBP protein levels during muscle differentiation (Figure 8).
evidence: This is inferred from the coordinated changes in Huwe1 and USP10 levels and their effects on TBP, as shown in Figures 5B, 7D, and modeled in Figure 8.

claim: The protein levels of TBP and TAFs are significantly down-regulated during terminal differentiation while other core pre-initiation complex components such as RNA Pol II remain largely unaffected.
source: One striking observation is that although the protein levels of TBP and TAFs are significantly down-regulated, the protein levels of other basal transcription factors like RNA polymerase II remain largely unchanged (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly shown by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In addition to the loss or depletion of TBP during terminal differentiation, one of the 'orphan TAFs' such as TAF3 and TAF7l becomes up-regulated or remains highly expressed while the other prototypic TFIID subunits become down-regulated.
source: In several previous studies, we observed that in addition to the loss or depletion of TBP during terminal differentiation of cell-types including myotubes and adipocytes, one of the so-called 'orphan TAFs' such as TAF3 and TAF7l, respectively, becomes up-regulated or remains highly expressed while the other prototypic TFIID subunits become down-regulated (Deato and Tjian, 2007; Yao et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies from the authors' lab.

claim: TRF3 appeared to play some role in possibly either substituting for TBP or otherwise remaining detectable during myoblast to myotube terminal differentiation.
source: In the case of myoblast to myotube formation, we also detected the presence of a TBP related factor, TRF3, that appeared to play some role in possibly either substituting for TBP, as seen by in vitro reactions, or otherwise remaining detectable during terminal differentiation (Deato and Tjian, 2007; Deato et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies from the authors' lab.

claim: In several cell types including ESCs, adipocytes and motor neurons, the emergence and up-regulation of orphan TAFs (i.e. TAF3, TAF7l and TAF9b) was observed but no up-regulation of TRFs was detected.
source: However, in several subsequent studies including ESC's, adipocytes and motor neurons, although we consistently observed the emergence and up-regulation of orphan TAFs (i.e. TAF3, TAF7l and TAF9b), we did not detect any up-regulation of TRFs (Liu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013; Herrera et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies from the authors' lab.

claim: ChIP-seq experiments suggested that orphan TAFs were associated both with core promoters (i.e. TSS) as well as either distal or proximal enhancers of target genes.
source: Instead, in each of these cases, ChIP-seq experiments suggested that these orphan TAFs were associated both with core promoters (i.e. TSS) as well as either distal or proximal enhancers of target genes (Liu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013; Herrera et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous ChIP-seq studies.

claim: KO mice lacking TRF3 showed no obvious muscle development phenotypes.
source: It was also reported that KO mice lacking TRF3 showed no obvious muscle development phenotypes casting doubt on the importance of TRF3 in muscle development in vivo (Gazdag et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The loss of TBP and TFIID components in certain cell-types is often accompanied by persistent or differential up-regulation of an orphan TAF.
source: In any case, in all our studies of terminal differentiating cell types, we observed a significant, sometimes dramatic loss of TBP and TFIID components that is often accompanied by persistent or differential up-regulation of an orphan TAF.
evidence: This is a summary of observations from multiple previous studies by the authors.

claim: Down-regulation of TBP protein levels could differentially affect genes with distinct TBP-promoter binding affinities.
source: An interesting possibility is that down-regulation of TBP protein levels could differentially affect genes with distinct TBP-promoter binding affinities.
evidence: This is speculation about a possible mechanism.

claim: Transcription factor temporal occupancies at high affinity sites are less sensitive to changes in concentration than those at low-affinity sites.
source: Recent single molecule studies suggest that transcription factor temporal occupancies at high affinity sites are less sensitive to changes in concentration than those at low-affinity sites (Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous single molecule study.

claim: By fine-tuning TBP protein levels, genes with weak TBP/TFIID binding promoters become selectively turned down while genes with strong TBP/TFIID binding promoters remain largely unaffected.
source: Thus, it is possible that, by fine-tuning TBP protein levels, genes with weak TBP/TFIID binding promoters become selectively turned down while genes with strong TBP/TFIID binding promoters remain largely unaffected thereby executing another mechanism for differential gene regulation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the cited single molecule study and the authors' observations.

claim: Purified His-Huwe1 binds to full-length TBP protein.
source: To confirm that this ubiquitination reaction requires direct physical interaction between TBP and Huwe1, we tested whether these two proteins coprecipitate through GST pull down experiments. Indeed, purified His-Huwe1 bound to full-length TBP protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is directly shown by GST pull-down data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The interaction between Huwe1 and TBP is dependent on the C-terminal DNA binding domain of TBP.
source: Moreover, this interaction is dependent on the C-terminal DNA binding domain of TBP, which is a highly conserved and highly structured region (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by testing TBP domain constructs in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The C-terminal DNA binding domain of TBP is a highly conserved and highly structured region.
source: Moreover, this interaction is dependent on the C-terminal DNA binding domain of TBP, which is a highly conserved and highly structured region (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TBP structure.

claim: Huwe1 contains a HECT domain which accepts ubiquitin from an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme in the form of a thioester, and then directly transfers the ubiquitin to targeted substrates.
source: Previous studies showed that Huwe1 contains a HECT (Homologous to the E6-AP Carboxyl Terminus) domain, which accepts ubiquitin from an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme in the form of a thioester, and then directly transfers the ubiquitin to targeted substrates (Rotin and Kumar, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HECT domain E3 ligases, supported by citation.

claim: The mCherry/sfGFP intensity ratio at steady state correlates with the half-life of the fusion protein, independent of the protein synthesis rate.
source: Due to the slow maturation rate of mCherry relative to sfGFP, the mCherry/sfGFP intensity ratio at steady state correlates with the half-life of the fusion protein, independent of the protein synthesis rate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is the principle of the fluorescent timer assay, supported by citation to the method.

claim: The target specificity of the ubiquitination system is largely determined by E3 ligases.
source: Ubiquitination is catalyzed by a cascade of three different enzymes, E1 activation enzyme, E2 conjugation enzymes and E3 ligases. The target specificity of the system is largely determined by E3 ligases, that recognize specific substrates for ubiquitination (Nakayama and Nakayama, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ubiquitination system, supported by citation.

claim: Ubiquitination is catalyzed by a cascade of three different enzymes: E1 activation enzyme, E2 conjugation enzymes and E3 ligases.
source: Ubiquitination is catalyzed by a cascade of three different enzymes, E1 activation enzyme, E2 conjugation enzymes and E3 ligases. The target specificity of the system is largely determined by E3 ligases, that recognize specific substrates for ubiquitination (Nakayama and Nakayama, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ubiquitination system, supported by citation.

claim: Poly-ubiquitin chains on a substrate can be formed using any of the seven lysines in ubiquitin.
source: It was shown that poly-ubiquitin chains on a substrate can be formed using any of the seven lysines in ubiquitin, and specific ubiquitin chain topologies are linked to distinct biological pathways (Komander and Rape, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ubiquitin chain topology, supported by citation.

claim: Specific ubiquitin chain topologies are linked to distinct biological pathways.
source: It was shown that poly-ubiquitin chains on a substrate can be formed using any of the seven lysines in ubiquitin, and specific ubiquitin chain topologies are linked to distinct biological pathways (Komander and Rape, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ubiquitin chain topology, supported by citation.

claim: The major protein degradation pathway in eukaryotic cells is mediated by the ubiquitin/proteasome system (UPS).
source: Since the major protein degradation pathway in eukaryotic cells is mediated by the ubiquitin/proteasome system (UPS) (Hochstrasser, 1996; Hershko and Ciechanover, 1998), we treated post-mitotic myotubes with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 and checked whether TBP downregulation was affected.
evidence: This is established knowledge about protein degradation, supported by citations.

claim: Cell-type specific transcription programs have generally been considered to be dictated by classic sequence-specific transcription factors.
source: The main reason is that cell-type specific transcription programs have generally been considered to be dictated by classic sequence-specific transcription factors (Farnham, 2009), while the components of the core promoter recognition machinery such as TBP were thought to be largely invariant across different cell types (Thomas and Chiang, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about transcriptional regulation, supported by citations.

claim: The components of the core promoter recognition machinery such as TBP were thought to be largely invariant across different cell types.
source: The main reason is that cell-type specific transcription programs have generally been considered to be dictated by classic sequence-specific transcription factors (Farnham, 2009), while the components of the core promoter recognition machinery such as TBP were thought to be largely invariant across different cell types (Thomas and Chiang, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about transcriptional regulation, supported by citation.

claim: Various cell-type specific 'orphan' TAFs are switched on to help direct developmental gene expression and terminal differentiation program in conjunction with TBP downregulation.
source: In conjunction with TBP downregulation, various cell-type specific 'orphan' TAFs are switched on to help direct developmental gene expression and terminal differentiation program (D'Alessio et al., 2009; Goodrich and Tjian, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Myod1 and Mef2c showed a ~twofold decrease in expression levels in Huwe1 knockdown myoblasts.
source: However, it is worth noting that two important myogenic regulator genes, Myod1 and Mef2c, showed a ∼twofold decrease in expression levels in Huwe1 knockdown cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.
